target_customer: Data teams in life sciences and biotech that keep data in AWS S3 (customers listed include Allen Institute, Inari, Flagship Pioneering, Cellarity)
problem: Scattered files in S3 are hard to version, search and trust, so teams cannot reuse data or feed it to AI.
business_model: Open-core scientific data management platform deployed in the customer's AWS account, sold through AWS Marketplace
product_category: Data versioning and data catalog on S3

founders.name: Kevin Moore
founders.background_notes: YC page: enterprise data processing, processor and memory architectures, in-memory database software, cloud architecture.

technical_complexity.rationale: Python client, versioned package format, web catalog and cloud backend on S3; standard distributed-systems work with a niche data model.

defensibility.rationale: The core is open source, so lock-in comes from deployment inside customer accounts and stored package history.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Quilt became an AWS Advanced Technology Partner sold on AWS Marketplace, so AWS acted as a channel rather than a copier.

market_need_then: Teams moving data and machine learning workloads to S3 lacked versioning and discovery tools; the YC page describes S3 as git for data, the company's own framing.

branding.domain_note: Used quiltdata.com, which now redirects to quilt.bio.

identity.voice_and_tone: Scientific data management for AI-ready biology data

rebrands.why: Positioning shift toward life sciences; no announcement found, date unknown.

branding.community_and_virality: Open source quilt3 on GitHub and a Data Engineering Podcast episode.

brand_strength.rationale: Known in a narrow data engineering niche; the name is shared by several other companies named Quilt.

pivots.from: Python data packaging and versioning for S3 (git for data)
pivots.to: Scientific data management platform for life sciences on AWS
pivots.why: Not stated; a 2020 Dolthub post says Quilt moved toward data discovery on S3.

outcome_analysis: Quilt Data started as an open source git for data tool on S3 and has moved toward a scientific data management platform for life sciences, with named biotech customers and an AWS Marketplace listing. It is still active with the founding CEO, a team of about six on the YC page, and no public funding detail, so it looks like a small, durable niche company rather than a venture-scale outcome.
notes: Funding unverified: CB Insights shows 120K over 5 rounds, PitchBook and Tryfundable show 4.2M seed, with the latest round in May or June 2021 and investors such as Alumni Ventures, Vertex Ventures, Fuel Capital and Y Combinator; no press release found, so no round is recorded. Competitor list left empty: dated search found Pachyderm (initial release May 2016 per a 2020 Dolthub post) but no source dated near Winter 2016. The shard calls Winter 2016 while founded year 2015 comes from a directory listing. Search results for other companies named Quilt were excluded.
